thread.title: Apple stock slips as analysts say iPhone preorders appear stable or down from last year - MarketWatch

author: Emily Bary
title: Apple stock slips as analysts say iPhone preorders appear stable or down from last year - MarketWatch
text:
A few days after the iPhone XS and iPhone XS Max became available for preorder, financial analysts reported Monday that sales looked stable to slightly weaker against the iPhone X preorder numbers from a year ago.
Jun Zhang of Rosenblatt Securities wrote Monday that preorder levels for the iPhone XS and iPhone XS Max looked “weaker compared to iPhone X preorders” a year ago. His estimates are based on his analysis of iPhone wait times—a week or two for most regions—as well as his projected production volumes from manufacturers.
Don’t miss: Why would anybody buy the iPhone XS?
In general, he expects that Apple Inc. AAPL, -2.66% will produce 35 million to 36 million iPhone XS and XS Max devices combined in the September and December quarters, compared with 36 million iPhone X devices in the same period a year ago. He thinks that about 10 million iPhone XS and XS Max models will ship in the September quarter and that Apple will produce roughly 15 million in that time period.
Zhang has a buy rating at $200 target price on the stock.
Instinet analyst Jeffrey Kvaal was slightly more upbeat about preorder trends in a note titled “Steady as she Goes.”
He commented that both carrier promotions and shipment times are at similar levels this year compared with last year. The stable shipment times “suggest demand tracking to plan,” Kvaal wrote.
See also: iPhone XR creates some drama for Apple’s new lineup
Kvaal thinks that Apple expects that iPhone XS Max volumes will be 70% higher than XS volumes but noted that the company doesn’t appear to be planning for “slim availability” of any of the three phones it introduced last week .
He added that while wireless deals may, on the surface, look better this year than they did a year ago, Verizon Communications Inc. VZ, +0.27% and peers have a “major catch” in their offer for a $700 credit with the purchase of a new iPhone. Those offers are only available to customers who add an additional line “which we believe will limit their attractiveness,” according to Kvaal, who rates the stock at neutral with a $210 price target.
Read: New Apple Watch doesn’t have the feature most consumers want
Apple didn’t respond to MarketWatch’s request for comment on preorder trends.
Apple shares ended Monday down 2.7%, though the stock is up 36% over the past 12 months. The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.35% of which Apple is a component, has gained 17% in that time.
